liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer calls it one of the very best, comparable in inspiration to the 2/28/73 version on Dick's Picks 28 [16]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Reviewer calls it a monster and the centerpiece of the whole show [10]
- Reviewer notes the band did not play He's Gone for Pigpen at this show [13]

## The recordings

- **gd73-03-15.sbd.cotsman.14035.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 26 songs; 200 min; rated 3.41/5 by 17 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls it the worst-sounding recording on the site, suited only to completists; vocals are poor, though Garcia's guitar is relatively audible; Reviewer finds the sound quality of this recording poor; Audience portion is not worth having; soundboard portion is a must, despite mono sections, patches and channel drops [5][7][8][10][14]
- **gd73-03-15.aud.vernon.13468.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 26 songs; 193 min; rated 3/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls it the worst-sounding recording on the site, suited only to completists; vocals are poor, though Garcia's guitar is relatively audible [6]
- **gd1973-03-15.151902.SonyStereo.ECM.Moskal.t.flac16**: source not stated; 26 songs; 199 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]. Said about its sound: Uploader rates quality as fair for 1973; Bill Graham intro missing and a few seconds of Promised Land missing [3]
- **gd1973-03-15.136652.sbd.reelmaster.cassette.dat.sirmick.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 187 min; rated 2/5 by 3 [4]

## Around the show

- Attendee says it was the first show after Pigpen died; band mostly faced each other in a circle, playing for each other and him [7]
- Reviewer notes this was the band's first show after Pigpen's death, which they feel weighed on the band; performance seems unfocused [11]
- Reviewer says Pigpen's death hung over a lackluster performance, yet the band did not cancel the show [13]
- The concert was billed as 'A Swell Dance Concert' [3]
- Reviewer says the band was playing at a consistently high level, opening a run lasting through April 1 [8]
- Reviewer says a song was not played until 3/19/73 after Pigpen's death, and the 3/24/73 version carries intense emotion [12]
- Reviewer likens the Other One to the 2/28/73 Dick's Picks 28 version, and praises the jamming overall [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd73-03-15.sbd.cotsman.14035.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [1]. Also: Composite of an audience source and a soundboard source, the latter via JackeySack, Matt Vernon and Paul Hartman; edited and encoded by JCotsman [1]
- **gd73-03-15.aud.vernon.13468.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Unknown; source: Audience Recording [2]
- **gd1973-03-15.151902.SonyStereo.ECM.Moskal.t.flac16**: taped by Gerry Moskal; transferred by Gerry Moskal Master Cassette Transfer->RR ->Cassette (Circa 1984)  Transfer/Flac Conversion 02-27-21 Brian Mandel  Cassette Transfer Maxell XL11-S90 Nakamichi BX300->SONY PCM-M10 16bit 44 Wave CD Wave Editor -> TLH->Flac; source: Sony Stereo ECM -->SONY TCD126 Location: TBD [3]
- **gd1973-03-15.136652.sbd.reelmaster.cassette.dat.sirmick.flac16**: taped by Anonomous; transferred by SIRMick; source: Source: Soundboard > Reel Master > Cassette > DAT (48k) [4]

## Art and photos
